text:
Sterile normal saline (0.9% sodium chloride) at room temperature is the standard bladder washout solution. Sterile water must not be used because it is hypotonic and can cause hemolysis, and the team note about chilled irrigant doesn't match standard practice, since cold fluid risks hypothermia and bladder spasm. Antiseptic or antibiotic additives are used only when a prescriber orders them, and volume and technique should follow facility protocol and the prescriber's order.
